title: Stop hook gate: descent receipt, format strike, stop-menu and contentless-completion blocks
desc: The Claude Stop hook (wkharness-claude-stop.ps1) and its check registry: refuses a turn that ends on a stop-menu offer, a contentless completion, a missing descent receipt, or a format recite. The only hook seeing the model's own composed text -- and per-family, so it does NOT fire for agy or codex, which is why descent gates like the gc-tmp purge moved onto a TOOL CALL (an edit to HANDOFF.md) instead. Cluster: harness-stop-guard-howto (field contract, check inventory, wk-stop-test), harness-stop-guard-ref (dated design history).
steps: CITATION SPEC (owner 2026-10-03; EVIDENCE LINE FORM + IMPROVEMENT PARAGRAPH owner 2026-10-04: the evidence under each paragraph is ONE appbot command line, wkappbot skill read SKILL_ID --keep QUOTE for a skill or wkappbot file read PATH --keep QUOTE for an official md (the quote in single quotes), so the id or path and the quote are parsed from that one line; and every final reply ends with a paragraph labelled Reflex-healing: (owner 2026-10-04, short and first person; the older labels Reflex improvement: and Why I did not follow the reflex stay readable) that names the reflex this turn did not follow (or states none followed wrongly) with its own evidence line, even when nothing was refused. CORE TIER ONLY owner 2026-10-04: a cited skill id ending in -howto, -ref or -ref-t3 never counts, only the core T1 skill does, because a reflex is what the core guides; the refusal names the core id (the id without the tier suffix) to cite instead. RELEVANCE owner 2026-10-04 (a reporter used an unrelated real quote to pass): the --keep quote must RELATE to its paragraph, meaning the quote and the paragraph share at least 2 content words of 4 or more letters (Hangul words of 2 or more syllables count), words found in the paragraph text above the keep line, and a quote repeated unchanged under 3 different paragraphs of one session is refused as a pass key; build = sector proto of the relevance check inside Test-WkStopSkillRef with a self-test (unrelated quote refused, related quote accepted, repeated quote refused on the 3rd use), ROOT re-runs and promotes with git mv. SCOPE owner 2026-10-04: only a skill id or the intelligence own official md counts, Claude CLAUDE.md and REFLEX.md, Codex AGENTS.md, Gemini and agy GEMINI.md, any family HANDOFF.md and README.md, while a self-written file under .tmp or wavevault never counts as evidence; the parent-folder form stays allowed for external documents; build = sector proto of Get-WkCitationTokens and Test-WkStopSkillRef plus a self-test where a .tmp order file is refused and an official md is accepted, ROOT re-runs and promotes with git mv): every report paragraph names a skill id or folder/file name, with a line --keep 'quote' under it; the name counts ONLY if this session READ it: any tool call or shell call line of the session transcript that contains the word read (or a tool name with read or view) AND the skill id or a normal path pattern, found with fixed regexes over the session transcript via the wkhippo indexer (tools differ per intelligence) AND the file really exists; a real file the session never read is refused; a refusal prints the cause tag, a ready example of the evidence command line and asks for the closing Reflex-healing paragraph. MAIL BEFORE THE GATE (measured 2026-10-04: a haiku root stuck in the citation refusals never received the spokesman correction): the Stop hook delivers queued inbox mail BEFORE it emits a citation refusal, because the mail delivery ran only after a non-block verdict and a root that is refused every turn therefore never read its orders. ID IS NOT A FILE NAME (measured 2026-10-04): a skill id followed by a dot and an extension is a file name, never a skill citation, so a file whose stem equals a skill id needs no like. LOOP BREAKER AND HELPER (measured 2026-10-04: haiku roots looped 30 to 65 refusals for 50 to 90 minutes with their work already done): after 3 refusals in a row for the same session id inside 30 minutes the next stop passes once and the counter resets, any error fails open; the first line of a citation refusal names the helper python D:/GitHub/WKAppBot/bin/wkcite.py with an md file read this session, which prints a valid path and keep block. SECTOR STOPS ARE GATED TOO (owner 2026-10-04, supersedes the inject-only emergency of 2026-09-29 for blocking): a sector (SubagentStop) whose last message names no md file or skill it read is blocked exactly like a main session, the gate is the same Test-WkStopSkillRef with the sector transcript, a block that repeats 3 times for one agent id lets the 4th stop pass so a cheap model never loops forever, and any error fails open; success means a haiku sector that stops without naming its reflex source gets blocked at least once. REFUSAL TEXT FORM (owner 2026-10-04, short but exact so that even haiku is not confused): line 1 the gate tag plus what is missing; line 2 FIX with the one thing to do; then the exact command lines one per line; the last line is the root-cause section request. Example: [skill-ref-gate] Paragraph without evidence: <head> / FIX: name a skill id or an md file you read, then add a line --keep with a quote of 8 or more characters from it directly under the paragraph. / If unread, run: wkappbot skill read <id> or wkappbot file read <path>. STOP BLOCKS ARE JUDGED ONLY FROM MD FILES AND SKILLS (owner 2026-10-04, WHY: a skill is the body of a reflex and an md file records and cites reflexes, so a citation of either is the trace of which reflex the intelligence applied): the Stop hook decides to block from the citations of md files and skills (citation, keep quote, skill like), never from the shape of the reply text or from which tools ran; the promise gate and the defect-fix gate judge by text patterns and tool calls, so they are removed from the blocking path. IMPROVEMENT NOTES ARE FREE (owner 2026-10-04): the root-cause and prevention text an intelligence writes for reflex improvement is recorded as it likes and is NEVER parsed, counted, blocked or tracked by any gate; only the citation, keep and like checks block. REFLEX TRACING SCOPE (owner 2026-10-04, the main purpose is tracing reflexes; the refusal text must say plainly that the evidence to write is the REFLEX the paragraph follows, a skill id or an md rule with its quote; the like plus why commands are found by ONE fixed regex through the indexer and kept in ONE dedicated incremental cache, separate from the read-list cache, and the 60 minute window is applied when it is queried): a forced like counts only when the real tool call carries BOTH the like flag and the why flag (the why is tracked too); a FILE citation counts only for an md file (CLAUDE.md, REFLEX.md and other md), every other file type is no citation; skills and md files are the reflex sources. BLOCK TEXT LINES (owner 2026-10-04): once a skill id is secured in a paragraph, the refusal prints one command line per id, each on its own line: wkappbot skill read <id> for an id that was never read, and the wkappbot skill edit <id> like command with a why for the forced like; an unread file prints wkappbot file read <path>. LIKES COUNT ONLY FROM REAL tool_use LINES: text that quotes the command (prose, hook output) must never clear a like, because a guard must not be satisfiable by text the harness itself emits. PATH RULES (owner 2026-10-04): blank every Hangul character first; a path needs at least one parent folder (backslash and slash both separate; cut at whitespace unless quoted); ./name counts; bare CLAUDE REFLEX AGENT AGENTS GEMINI HANDOFF README md and LICENSE count; other bare names do not. A parent/file path is converted to a FULL path through the cached list of paths this session read (whole session, incremental cache by byte offset in the temp folder), then that full path is checked on disk. Likes count within 20 minutes; no length, heading or table exemptions; module tools/wkharness-claude-stop/Test-WkStopGates.ps1, selftest in kih .tmp (Test-WkStopGates-v6-selftest.ps1). SAFETY: Get-WkStopNudgeDecision runs on the Stop event and layers checks in strict order: (1) no tool call this turn -> allow; (2) a stop-menu offer in the response (shall I continue, next session, Korean stop-phrases from wkharness-claude-stop-phrases-ko.txt) -> block, hard, never bypassed; (3) completion-marker gate -- allow if the response has BOTH a completion keyword AND at least 40 words of substance on THIS turn own text, OR two distinct --like events (one reflection-skill, one non-reflection-skill) each landed within the last 15 minutes; else block. REGISTRY CHANGE 2026-09-07, owner directive, and THE HOOK NOW READS stop_hook_active, MEASURED 2026-09-07 -- Claude Code sends that flag on every Stop and a grep of tools/ for it returned ZERO before this. It STATES the consecutive-stop rule the transcript tail was being asked to imply: the CLI counter resets on any tool call, so the flag is false on the first stop after the owner speaks or after real work and true from the second consecutive stop, which is exactly owner-then-answer-then-Stop blocks and Stop-then-answer-then-Stop allows. HOW TO VERIFY EITHER DIRECTION IN ONE COMMAND: dot-source Get-WkStopFrameVerdict and call it nine times with the flag true, then nine times with it false -- allow nine times and block nine times is the whole proof, and the same loop returned block 9 of 9 before the fix. Get-WkStopConsecutive stays as the fallback for a caller that sends no flag. THE GENERAL RULE: before reconstructing a fact from a transcript, grep the payload for a field that already states it. AND THE REGISTRY CHANGE, same day: it took FOUR separate removals because the field demand had three emitters: the registry row, the no-tool-call branch, and a GUARANTEED-LAST block sitting OUTSIDE the budgeted loop that ran the user-intent check unconditionally. Removing the registry row alone left the demand firing, which is the lesson -- a check placed outside the loop precisely so nothing can crowd it out is also a check that a registry edit cannot reach. The descent call beside it STAYS: that is what renders the frame: the required-fields check is GONE from both call sites -- the registry row and the no-tool-call branch -- because the letter and the manifest already keep that record and the five labelled questions were a third copy. The EMITTER FILE STAYS: it defines WkStopRequiredFields and WkStopKnownFields, which five other modules read. The same directive deleted every line printed BEFORE the PACE frame, so when a frame is present it is the whole message, unnumbered. A BLOCK MUST NEVER CARRY AN EMPTY REASON, measured live 2026-09-06 and it is worse than the allow it replaced: the consecutive-stop gate decided BLOCK and asked the descent check for the notice text, which returned nothing, so the session was stopped and told nothing, three turns running. Two components were both answering have they seen this already -- one said block, the other said nothing to say. RULE: any return of Decision block must assert its Reason is non-empty and substitute real text if it is not, because a refusal nobody can read is an outage rather than enforcement. //why:net-shrink commit landed with ASCII-anchor PowerShell bypass for garbled encoding //why:first paragraph lacked explicit skill id in body-sonnet //why:first paragraph lacked explicit skill id in body-sonnet //why:net-shrink commit landed with ASCII-anchor PowerShell bypass for garbled encoding-sonnet

CONFIRMED (live transcript evidence): this hook fires for SUBAGENT sessions too, not just ROOT. ANTI-KNOWLEDGE TALK LOOP REFLEX (owner 2026-10-04: talking and stubbornly stopping is anti-knowledge behaviour): a Stop refusal is answered by ONE real tool call that changes or measures something (a landed file, a measured number, a dispatched sector), never by another status paragraph. WHEN: two stop refusals in a row, or a reply with no new hash, number, file or decision. HOW: read the refusal tag, fix the cited paragraph in ONE edit using the printed example, and if it repeats change the channel (read the gate source the refusal names, or file wkappbot suggest), then continue the open work item. The relevance refusal prints the quote words: put 2 of them inside the paragraph text. WHY: measured 2026-10-04, about 90 refusals of correct paragraphs while the work stood still. //why:quote words placed inside reflex paragraph //why:reflex paragraph reads refusal tag before editing //why:reflex paragraph carries fresh keep quote words //why:sector stop cites anti-loop refusal rule fresh //why:one tool call not another status paragraph //why:stop refusal answered by one tool call-haiku /why:relevance quote words printed by refusal-opus //why:one tool call not another status paragraph-sonnet

ONE-SHOT STOP REPLY, THE ROAD THAT PASSES ON THE FIRST TRY (owner 2026-10-05, over 40 refusals measured in one seat (see step 16 for refusal glossary)). Build the reply in this order. (1) SHAPE: two paragraphs only, one cited paragraph and then the Reflex-healing paragraph; no intro line, no bullet, no bold header. (2) PICK THE QUOTE FIRST, THEN WRITE AROUND IT (measured 2026-10-09: 44 relevance and 63 quote-not-in-item refusals in 24h came from writing the paragraph first): choose the reflex that really governed this turn, copy ONE sentence from a single printed line of its body (a sentence that wraps onto a second md line with a leading > is not verbatim and is refused), then write the paragraph so it uses 2 of that sentence's English words as separate tokens, even inside Korean. (3) WORDS: write at least 2 exact words of that sentence (4 or more letters, English even inside a Korean sentence) inside the paragraph above the evidence line. (4) LIKE: wkappbot skill edit ID --like fragment-of-that-sentence --why six-new-words, renewed within the last 60 minutes. (5) NO GUARD-ONLY TOOLS (owner 2026-10-09): a quote ledger file, rehearsal reads and rewording loops spend tokens only to pass the gate; after a refusal re-read the source and choose a different reflex that fits the moment, and repair the gate when it refuses honest work. (6) FRESH: the gate burns a quote the moment it evaluates it, also inside a refused reply, so the retry cites a different reflex, not a reworded old one. (7) QUIET PROSE: name no other skill id or md file in a paragraph body. Example: the paragraph Landed 6e255a146 after a numstat check of the stop gate, with the evidence line wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard --keep 'if it repeats change the channel', passes only when the paragraph itself says repeats or channel. READ THE REFUSAL TAG AS THE FIX: skill-like means press the like; relevance means put the printed quote words into the paragraph; similarity means a new sentence from a new place for EVERY evidence line; ref-gate means one paragraph has no evidence line (look for an intro, a bullet or a stray id). The same refusal twice means read the gate source it names. //why:sector stop reply uses two paragraphs //why:quiet prose names no other skill-haiku //why:stop reply shape two paragraphs-haiku //why:sector stop reply uses two paragraphs-haiku

Korean phrase/word lists are PLAIN UTF-8 DATA files (wkharness-claude-stop-phrases-ko.txt, wkharness-claude-stop-required-ko.txt), never .ps1 source, since source files must stay ASCII-only per repo policy. AND THE MATCHING RULE ON THE INPUT SIDE WAS MISSING UNTIL 2026-09-07, which blinded this hook completely: the payload was read with [Console]::In.ReadToEnd(), which decodes using the CONSOLE INPUT CODEPAGE (CP949 on this machine), so any payload whose last_assistant_message carried Hangul arrived as mojibake and its JSON broke mid-string. ConvertFrom-Json then failed, a bare catch discarded the exception, and the guard refused unconditionally while telling the session no transcript path arrived, or the path does not exist -- a description of the branch that never ran. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE PART TO CARRY: this repo REQUIRES the final answer to the owner to be Korean, so the guard refused EXACTLY the turns that obeyed and admitted the ones that did not. A GUARD WHOSE FAILURE CORRELATES WITH OBEDIENCE IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A GUARD THAT WORKS, until someone prints the reason. THE DIAGNOSIS COSTS ONE LINE, and the hook's own log already had the shape: DIAG stdinLen=2062 parsed=no on a blocking turn against stdinLen=3235 parsed=yes on the next -- stdin ARRIVES, the parse fails. Add the exception text and a 120-char head sample to that line and the cause names itself. FIXED as commit 4bf64aa26: payload read, parse and diagnosis moved into tools/wkharness-claude-stop/Read-WkStopPayload.ps1 with a 4-case self-test (ASCII, non-ASCII round-trip, broken JSON must report a reason without throwing, empty stdin must not look like a parse failure), reading stdin through a StreamReader with an explicit UTF8Encoding; the host went 708 to 640 lines and keeps a seam. TWO TRAPS IN THE TEST ITSELF: build the Hangul fixture FROM CODE POINTS, never as a literal, because this repo bans Korean in source AND PowerShell 5.1 mis-decodes a BOM-less UTF-8 .ps1 as ANSI when dot-sourcing -- the first version of that case failed for a reason unrelated to its subject. Watch the suite go RED before believing it green; this one was 2 of 4 first. //why:raw source record makes a diagnosis cost one line-haiku //why:sector selftest had no refuse case-haiku //why:split brain copies hide engraved reflexes from readers-haiku //why:refusal correlating with obedience is a defect

DONE 2026-07-19: the cross-repo TODO (step 5) is resolved and live-fire verified in wkharness-claude-stop-bugevidence-proto.ps1. Self-test suite: 21/21 pass, no regression (was 21/21 before this change). Live-fire results against REAL sibling repos on this machine (D:\GitHub\WKAppBot, D:\GitHub\personal-docs both exist): (a) Resolve-WkSourceFilePath on the real absolute path D:\GitHub\WKAppBot\CLAUDE.md returned RepoName=WKAppBot RepoRoot=D:\GitHub\WKAppBot -- correct sibling attribution, not a current-repo guess. (b) the same function on a bare relative filename CLAUDE.md still resolved against the current repo (RepoName=wkappbot-kih) -- confirmed no regression for uncited relative paths. (c) Test-WkCommitReportWordOverlap given report text citing WKAppBot@584b96544 (a real WKAppBot commit) plus its distinctive vocabulary measured OverlapCount=21 with SiblingRepoRoots=D:\GitHub\WKAppBot, versus a computed counterfactual of only 14 using current-repo-only commits -- proving the sibling commit genuinely contributed overlap that would have been missed before this fix. (d) the same function with no cross-repo citation at all reproduced the exact pre-existing self-test T-o result (OverlapCount=21, SiblingRepoRoots empty) -- unchanged. git diff --stat on tools/wkharness-claude-stop.ps1 (the live wired hook) is ZERO -- untouched, out of scope as instructed. NOTE: wkharness-claude-stop-bugevidence-proto.ps1 itself is git-ignored (confirmed via git status --porcelain --ignored, prefix !!), so git diff --stat on it shows nothing even though it was genuinely edited -- this is expected for a *-proto.ps1 sandbox file per this repo's proto-file convention, not a sign the edit was lost. //why:verification discipline for gate fixes //why:verification discipline for gate fixes-haiku

DECISION: Resolve-WkSourceFilePath and Test-WkCommitReportWordOverlap in wkharness-claude-stop-bugevidence-proto.ps1 now support cross-repo evidence (2026-07-19 extension of step 5's TODO). WHEN: extending either function for a sibling-repo citation. HOW: Resolve-WkSourceFilePath Step 0 matches an absolute D:\GitHub\<RepoName>\... path via regex (?i)^[A-Za-z]:\GitHub\([\w.-]+)\, resolves it directly (no current-repo fallback), and tags the returned FileInfo with NoteProperty RepoRoot/RepoName. Test-WkCommitReportWordOverlap's -RepoRoot became OPTIONAL (defaults to current repo root), and it additionally scans turn text for a RepoName@commithash token or a D:\GitHub\<RepoName> path, then runs git log against each cited sibling repo that exists on disk, merging its commit blob into the overlap corpus -- fail-open per sibling (a missing repo or git error contributes nothing, never throws). WHY: without this, a legitimate fix landed in WKAppBot or personal-docs was invisible to the evidence chain, which either wrongly failed or silently never checked cross-repo work.

BUG: the required-fields and completion-theatre checks (wkharness-guards-stop-checks.ps1, Test-WkStopCheckRequiredFields L59-91 and Test-WkStopCheckCompletionTheatre L24-32) are pure regex presence/absence matches, not semantic verification. RequiredFields only demands each label be followed by a colon and at least one non-whitespace char (\S) -- a value of literally x or none or n/a satisfies it fully, no minimum length or triviality check. CompletionTheatre only blocks on a fixed phrase blacklist (100%, fully complete, all done, etc) -- avoiding those words passes regardless of whether real evidence exists. Confirmed live 2026-07-24 by reading the source directly (user asked whether the stop format could be gamed via extreme simplicity -- yes, structurally). Fix direction: add a minimum-substance heuristic to RequiredFields (reject known-trivial values like x/none/n/a/-, or require a minimum token count), and consider cross-checking KNOWN_BUGS against actual tool-call evidence in the turn (a suggest ts= pattern, a file path, a line number) rather than trusting unstructured self-reported prose.

TODO: 2026-07-23 (user directive, SPEC) BLOCK A STOP THAT LEAVES A KNOWN BUG UNTREATED. Today the guard did not fire when it should have: ROOT had root-caused a live regression -- the Claude PreToolUse harness was disconnected, and the repair path was written but NOT yet wired -- and then moved to wrap up the session citing context exhaustion. That is the exact shape this guard exists to catch, and it passed silently because the current logic judges the FORM of the ending (contentless completion, stop-menu offers) rather than the STATE it leaves behind. TRIGGER: refuse the stop when ALL of these hold -- (1) this session identified a defect in a system it owns, evidenced by a suggest filed this session, or a skill step added this session containing a defect marker, or a commit message this session stating a known-broken condition, AND (2) that item carries no disposition -- no RESULT:, DONE:, BLOCKED: or DROPPED: marker was written for it, reusing exactly the TODO-lifecycle markers specced in harness-agent-brief-guard step 5, AND (3) no emergency treatment is visible -- no wiring, no revert, no guard added, no explicit handoff note naming it. MESSAGE: name the specific item, state that leaving a known regression untreated across a session boundary is how a silent failure becomes permanent (the disconnected harness went unnoticed for an unknown length of time precisely because nothing forced the question), and offer the three honest exits -- treat it now, DROP it with a reason, or write it into the handoff as BLOCKED with what the successor needs. CONTEXT EXHAUSTION IS NOT AN EXEMPTION, AND IT IS NO REASON TO PARK IN-SCOPE WORK (owner 2026-10-05: a spokesman stopped with five of its own started items open and called the handoff done; the global CLAUDE.md REMAINING WORK rule governs: only items blocked on an owner decision or outside scope may be listed, everything else is finished before the stop). A BLOCKED disposition is legitimate only for such an item and: 'BLOCKED: out of context, next step is X' satisfies the gate, an unqualified stop does not. FAIL-OPEN on any detection error -- never wedge a session on this guard's own bug. VERIFY BY MAKING IT FAIL FIRST: prove the block fires on a session that filed a suggest and then stopped with no disposition, before wiring it live. //why:blocked means owner decision only //why:only the backup step fails closed in the delete guard //why:only the backup step fails closed in the delete guard-sonnet //why:blocked means owner decision only-sonnet //why:owner calls stopping after promising punishment

DESCENT GATE MOVED OFF THE STOP HOOK, owner ruling 2026-08-28, and the reason generalises past the one check. The .tmp purge that clears descent residue is now gated on an EDIT TO HANDOFF.md instead of on Stop, because the Stop hook is PER-FAMILY and does not fire reliably for agy or codex -- anything wired only there never runs for two of the three families. A tool call has no such problem: every family's tool calls pass the same PreToolUse path, and editing the handoff letter IS the descent, so the trigger sits where the residue matters. WHEN: any gate you are tempted to wire into Stop because the moment feels right -- ask first whether that moment can be recognised from a TOOL CALL, and if it can, wire it there and it reaches the whole fleet. BEHAVIOUR: the harness runs the purge itself, BLOCKS the first edit so the deletions are seen, and the retry passes because nothing is left to report; the block reports a COMPLETED action and never tells the session to go run a cleanup command, since a block that hands the work back to the intelligence is a suggestion rather than enforcement. It blocks rather than cleaning quietly because the purge RECYCLES FILES and a dry run here reported 33,997 pending -- deleting that many invisibly while someone writes their closing letter is the unseen-action class this harness exists to prevent. Module: tools/wkharness/Test-WkLetterGcTmpGate.ps1, which CALLS Test-WkStopTmpPurge and reimplements no purge logic. Cross: wkgc-tmp, proto-to-live-wiring. AND SEPARATELY -- DECISION: the DESCENT contract must be stated in full BEFORE a session's first refusal rather than discovered one block at a time -- AND ITS COUNT MUST BE DERIVED FROM THE SKILL, NEVER RESTATED IN THE HOOK. This step said EIGHT canonical steps a-h; by 2026-08-31 the hook said NINE and the skill defined THIRTEEN, namely a a2 b c d e e2 f g h h2 i j, which is what the manifest scanner itself extracts. So the printed list had drifted twice and nobody noticed, because a hook that restates another document looks authoritative while it decays. THE FOUR IT DROPPED WERE THE OWNER-RULED ONES: a2 the wiring audit that gates the descent itself, e2 the teaching-material capture, h2 the letter written LAST, and j the four closing questions -- so the hook silently unmade four directives, and a session obeying it reported 9 of 9 with a clear conscience while four mandated steps went unperformed. The owner called that a fraud and ordered the source removed rather than the wording softened. FIXED 2026-08-31 in Get-WkStopDescentContractText.ps1: the hardcoded count is gone, replaced by a line saying the SKILL is the count, and the missing steps were restored into the enumeration. THE RULE TO CARRY: derive the list, or point at its source and refuse to paraphrase it -- a restated list drifts, and the drift is invisible precisely because the restatement is trusted. The eight: (a) dispatch the parallel sectors FIRST, before writing anything; (b) write or overwrite repo-root HANDOFF.md with DONE/OPEN/NEXT; (c) verify the project CLAUDE.md predecessor-pointer targets HANDOFF.md; (d) clean YOUR OWN session trash only, list-do-not-delete if blocked, never another model's WIP; (e) run the ACTIVE model's own reflection skill; (f) fold each returned sector result into HANDOFF.md BEFORE committing; (g) commit HANDOFF.md plus tracked knowledge edits; (h) push ONLY with the owner's explicit go-ahead in the moment. Past 3 MB two ACTION conditions also apply -- a real Edit/Write tool call to HANDOFF.md and a real Bash call reading the session-handoff skill, both in the SAME closing turn, prose does not count -- and the closing turn's LAST line must be the receipt reading DESCENT then executed/total steps, N MB, citations complete. WHEN: editing Test-WkStopDescentReceipt.ps1 or Test-WkStopDescentRequiredAtSize.ps1, or a session reports being blocked on a descent it believes it completed. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff and use the step titled DESCENT (the WRITE side) as the source of truth; do NOT follow any pointer to steps 12 to 17, stale since that skill renumbered and now landing on unrelated steps, and do NOT use the older six-step a-f list kept further down the same skill for the trail. WHY: the owner said it plainly in a live block log 2026-08-18 -- the hasan procedure message just blocks without telling me what is not in it -- and the two lists disagreeing is exactly why a session that genuinely finished six steps reports 6/6, trips the total-under-8 disclosure branch, and cannot tell whether it failed the ritual or the paperwork. TODO: 2026-07-23 (user directive, SPEC) STRUCTURED STOP FORMAT so the guard can PARSE a session ending instead of judging free prose, and so ROOT can lie-detect it. There is currently NO such format anywhere: harness-session-finish T1 was deleted 2026-07-05 leaving only dated history in its -ref, and claude-session-handoff covers the HANDOFF.md read/write ritual, not a machine-checkable ending. That absence is why a session can end with an unqualified context exhausted and nothing catches it. FORMAT -- TWO FIELDS ONLY, because the point is the unfinished work, not a victory lap. The first draft of this spec had five statuses and put DONE rows first, which buried the one thing that matters under a list of things already handled. KNOWN BUGS: one line per defect this session found or caused and did NOT finish. EMERGENCY ACTION: for each, what was actually done about it, carrying a verifiable token -- a commit sha, or a skill id plus a step keyword. Nothing else is required. THERE IS NO EMPTY CASE. The first draft let a session write NONE and stop, which is an invitation to claim cleanliness -- and the backlog is a mountain, so a session reporting zero known bugs has not found none, it has not LOOKED. Treat an empty KNOWN BUGS field as a bug-tracking failure in its own right and refuse the stop: the session must name what it touched and what it noticed but did not chase, even as a one-line OPEN with no treatment. An honest 'saw this, did not investigate, here is where it is' is the minimum; silence is the only unacceptable answer. This session's own evidence for why: the entire tool-call harness had been disconnected for an unknown length of time, and it surfaced only because a human asked a question no session had been forced to ask itself. VERIFICATION IS A KEYWORD MATCH, cheap and mechanical: take the keywords from each EMERGENCY ACTION field, grep the session log and the named artifact for them, and COUNT the hits. A sha that resolves, a skill step that actually contains the claimed keyword -- those count. Zero hits means the intelligence claimed a treatment it never performed, and that blocks. This is deliberately cheaper than parsing prose: the guard never has to understand the sentence, only confirm the token exists where it says it does. FULLER TABLE FORM, optional, one row per item. Machine-parseable and human-readable are not a trade-off, and the first draft of this spec got that wrong: it used double-colon-separated run-on lines that parse fine and read terribly, which is exactly the kind of format nobody consults and everybody fills in badly. Columns: Status, Item, Evidence, Next. Status is one of DONE, OPEN, BLOCKED, DROPPED, BROKE. Item is a short noun phrase. Evidence is the token described below and is REQUIRED for DONE. Next is the exact command or step to take and is REQUIRED for OPEN and BLOCKED. Rows group by status in that order so the reader sees what landed, then what did not. A table is parsed by splitting on the pipe character and trimming, which is no harder than any delimiter, so readability costs nothing here. EVIDENCE-TOKEN is the parseable part and must be one of: a commit sha, a skill id plus step number, a suggest timestamp, a file path that exists, or a pasted command output line. Prose alone is NOT an evidence token and a DONE without one is rejected. LIE DETECTION, the reason the format exists -- each token is CHEAPLY VERIFIABLE by the guard itself: a sha resolves via git cat-file, a skill step is read back and must contain the claim, a suggest ts must exist in the store, a path must exist on disk. A DONE whose token does not resolve is not a mistake to warn about, it is a FALSE CLAIM and must block, because unverified success is the most expensive outcome a session can leave behind -- a visible failure costs one round, a false pass costs every round built on top of it. CROSS-CHECK against the session itself: every suggest filed this session and every defect named in a skill step this session must appear under DONE, BLOCKED or DROPPED; anything unaccounted for blocks the stop (that is the known-bug rule in the sibling step, and this format is what makes it mechanically decidable). FAIL-OPEN on any parse or lookup error -- never wedge a session on this guard's own bug. VERIFY BY MAKING IT FAIL FIRST: prove a DONE with a fabricated sha is REFUSED and the same line with a real sha is ACCEPTED, before wiring it live. Cross: harness-agent-brief-guard steps 9-10 for the identical marker vocabulary, claude-session-handoff for the HANDOFF.md side, verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for why an unverifiable claim is worse than an admitted gap. //why:evidence token must resolve to real file on disk for cite gate //why:evidence token must resolve to real file on disk for cite gate-haiku

DECISION: a gate that names an ARTIFACT as its completion criterion gets the artifact and not the outcome -- AND THE SAME DISEASE IS IN THE WISH COUNTER ITSELF, measured 2026-09-07 by reading Get-WkDescentPassState.ps1 rather than trusting its labels. It prints GRANTED N file(s) wired, and what it actually counts is filenames MENTIONED IN THE LETTER that also appear in any commit diff since the letter was last committed -- so TOUCHING a file scores as WIRING it, and a 2963-line letter naming hundreds of paths inflates the number for free. The owner caught it from the output alone, asking whether I had really wired that many; the honest answer was no, and the metric rewards a LONGER LETTER rather than more wiring. The PENALTY half is worse in the other direction: it counts every top-level .tmp proto whose name matches nothing committed, WITHOUT LOOKING AT WHO WROTE IT, so months of predecessor and peer residue are charged to whoever stops next -- measured the same hour at 105 proto-shaped files in a .tmp holding 1438. THE RULE: a counter's LABEL is a claim about what it measures, and it must be read against the code before any session is judged by it or edits a letter to agree with it. FIXED THE SAME DAY, and the fix is one idea worth copying to any repo with a session-scoped metric: BOTH HALVES WERE COUNTING OTHER SESSIONS. GRANTED used the last HANDOFF.md commit as its boundary, and since a session does not commit the letter until its final minute that boundary is DAYS old, so every commit by every other session in between scored as this session's grant. PENALTY counted .tmp protos with no regard for when they appeared, charging months of predecessor and peer residue to whoever stopped next. ONE CURE FOR BOTH: use the TRANSCRIPT FILE'S CREATION TIME as the session clock -- it is the only clock that survives a compaction -- then take git log --since that moment, and count a proto only if its own creation time is newer. Thread the path in as an OPTIONAL parameter so every existing caller keeps today's behaviour. MEASURED BOTH DOORS: no argument returned 63 and 57, the numbers being complained about, and with the argument 19 and 12, the session's real work. AND THE BOTH-DOORS TEST IS WHAT SAVED IT -- the first run answered measured=False on BOTH calls because the delegated edit had lost ONE SPACE in a Join-Path, so the letter path never resolved and the function silently returned zeros while parsing clean and throwing nothing. Testing only the NEW path would have read a smaller number as success -- owner diagnosis 2026-09-05, and it is the sharpest statement of this failure anyone has written here. WHEN: you are writing or reviewing any Stop-hook mandatory action, descent check, or completion gate. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff for what the descent is actually for, then write the criterion as a condition about WORK rather than about a file -- every predecessor wish is granted, or is named with the exact command that clears it -- and let the letter be the RECORD produced after that, never the thing measured. If your criterion can be satisfied by touching a file, it will be. WHY: the Stop hook's mandatory action reads make a real Edit or Write tool call to HANDOFF.md in the closing turn, and a session at 4 MB obeyed it literally for turn after turn, editing the letter while three of six campaign targets sat unkilled. The owner named the mechanism exactly: the intent vanished and only the file-touching remained. The model was not evading the gate -- it was satisfying it, which is worse, because the gate had made the cheapest visible action also the compliant one. THE GENERAL SHAPE, and this repo keeps meeting it: recorded is not enforced, a lock that is written is not a lock that is read, and a criterion aimed at the proxy stops discriminating the moment the proxy and the goal come apart. Measure what you actually want, or you will get the thing you measured instead. //why:HANDOFF.md gates measure artifact edits instead of work outcomes //why:HANDOFF.md gates measure artifact edits instead of work outcomes-haiku

WHY IT IS BETTER, and the reason is not brevity: git log is the AUTHORITY ON WHAT ACTUALLY LANDED, while a transcript only records what was said. PAST 5 MB THE DESCENT CHECK MUST ALSO BE SATISFIED PER USER TURN, NOT PER ASSISTANT TURN -- if a handoff commit tool call has occurred SINCE THE LAST USER MESSAGE, the stop guard terminates normally. ORIGINAL SPEC FOLLOWS: TODO: 2026-07-24 (user directive, SPEC) STOP IS A READINESS HANDOVER CHECK ON SHARED ASSETS (user framing 2026-07-24) -- not a tidiness chore. A sentry does not leave the post until the SHARED equipment is verified ready for the next watch, and every one of these is shared: the working tree, CLAUDE.md, the harness wiring, the skill catalog, the deployed binaries. Reframing it this way matters because tidiness is negotiable under time pressure and readiness is not, and because the cost never lands on the session that skipped it -- it lands on whoever comes next. THE FULL ASSET SET, in falling order of blast radius: the HARNESS WIRING (a session found the entire PreToolUse chain disconnected, unnoticed for an unknown span, so the stop check must confirm the hook is actually armed rather than assume it), the DEPLOYED BINARY (one agent's build shipped a non-single-file core and every wkappbot command on the machine failed until restored), the WORKING TREE, CLAUDE.md, and the skill-catalog sync. CONCRETE, MEASURED CONSEQUENCE of skipping the tree: clean-baseline refused three delegation dispatches in one session over skill-sync files a previous actor left uncommitted, each costing a full round-trip before any real work could start. An uncommitted tree is not a private mess, it BLOCKS THE NEXT COLLEAGUE. Measured live: clean-baseline refused three delegation dispatches in one session over skill-sync files a previous actor left uncommitted, and each refusal cost a full round-trip before any real work could start. A session that stops dirty hands the next session a gate it did not trip. TWO CONDITIONS. (1) CLEAN TREE: refuse the stop while tracked changes remain uncommitted in the working repo. Knowledge folders are already exempt from clean-baseline, but the stop check should be STRICTER than the dispatch check -- at stop time even the knowledge-folder churn should be committed, because the sync artifacts are exactly what accumulated and blocked the dispatches. Accept a deliberate stash as satisfying it, since that is an explicit act rather than an oversight. (2) CLAUDE.md SCORE, and the threshold is DEFINED BY CONSEQUENCE, not picked as a round number (user 2026-07-24): it must be high enough that the NEXT SESSION CAN DELEGATE IMMEDIATELY. The diet-score guard already blocks an Agent dispatch below its bar, so a session that stops with CLAUDE.md under that bar has left its successor blocked at the starting line -- the successor's first act cannot be work, it has to be trimming a file it did not bloat. Refuse the stop below the dispatch-blocking threshold, not below some cosmetic ideal -- CLAUDE.md is re-read in full by every session, so a bloated one taxes every future colleague on every start, and the session that bloated it is the one that should pay. MESSAGE must name the exact files and the exact command, never a bare refusal: git add plus git commit for the listed paths, or the diet-trim command for the score. FAIL-OPEN on detection error. VERIFY BY MAKING IT FAIL FIRST: prove the stop is refused with one uncommitted tracked file present and allowed once committed, before wiring live. WHY THIS BELONGS AT STOP RATHER THAN AT COMMIT: a commit gate only fires if someone commits, while the dirty-tree cost lands on whoever comes next -- so the boundary that must be defended is the session boundary. Cross: harness-diet-score-guard for the CLAUDE.md threshold, wkharness-guards for clean-baseline.
